standard_paragraphs.label: NEW-Rood tiles heavier, internally shakes and new strutting suoport
standard_paragraphs.text: Over time, roofs on existing buildings will require replacement, and in most cases, such work will require Building Regulations approval. The roof coverings appear to have been replaced or re-covered at some point in the past, although the exact date could not be established. It is likely that the original roof covering comprised clay or slate tiles. The current interlocking concrete tiles are considerably heavier than traditional clay or slate tiles, which can result in overloading of the roof timbers. However, where visible, there were no excessive signs of deflection or distortion to the roof structure. That said, shakes were observed in some timbers, and additional strutting supports have been installed, suggesting the roof has experienced some minor movement in the past. Your legal adviser should confirm whether Building Regulations approval was obtained for these alterations (see more comments in Sections E1 and H1).

standard_paragraphs.label: unfelt not lapped inside of the gutter
standard_paragraphs.text: Where partially visible, we observed that the underfelt at the edges of the roof on the two-storey rear addition is not correctly lapped into the gutter. The primary function of roofing underfelt is to provide an additional layer of protection against water penetration. Properly lapping the felt into the rainwater gutter ensures that any water that gets beneath the roof tiles is directed into the gutter, preventing it from running down the fascia or into the building structure. If the roofing felt is not properly lapped into the gutter, water could potentially seep behind the gutter or into the wall structure, leading to dampness, rot, or other moisture-related issues. The underfelt should extend beyond the edge of the roof and into the gutter to ensure that water flows directly into the gutter. Care must be taken to avoid sagging of the felt, as this can cause water to pool and potentially overflow into unintended areas. If the underfelt is not properly supported and installed, it can "sag," causing rainwater to collect and allowing the leading edge of the felt to fall behind the gutter. Further investigation by a competent roofing contractor is recommended to carry out the necessary repairs and ensure the roof coverings are fully watertight. Additionally, the condition of the roof timbers at the edges of the roof should be checked to ensure there is no rot. Whist this work is not urgent; since no visible signs of water ingress were noted during our inspection, hidden defects may exist. It is advisable that when the roof is eventually replaced in the future, a complete overhaul of this area be carried out by a competent roofing contractor to ensure proper detailing and compliance with Building Regulations. Condition Rating 2.

standard_paragraphs.label: MAIN ROOF
standard_paragraphs.text: Whilst the subject unit is less likely to be directly affected by potential defects to the main roof, these could form part of a shared management commitment. We have not studied the lease. In any event, rights and responsibilities for maintenance should be investigated by your legal adviser. The main roof is a butterfly structure. The roof coverings could not be inspected as there was no available vantage point. This type of roof structure utilises horizontal valley gutters to aid rainwater runoff. These are usually concealed from view by parapet walls or the building’s façade. Valleys are always potential problem areas and should be regularly inspected and repaired as necessary. However, we could not inspect this section due to the lack of an available vantage point. Condition Rating: NI. Where visible from the rear communal garden, the mortar bedding in the roof verges showed signs of deterioration, with some areas of mortar missing, creating holes. Although this is less likely to affect the subject flat, over the long term, any potential water ingress could affect the roof structure or surrounding areas. Condition Rating: 2. The horizontal valley gutter between the pitched slopes could not be inspected due to the lack of an accessible vantage point. Access would require a long builder’s ladder, which falls outside the scope of this survey. Valley gutters are notoriously prone to leakage and should be fully inspected prior to any legal commitment to purchase. Even if in good condition, they can become blocked by leaves, snow, or ice, causing water to overflow and seep into the building’s structure. Condensation on the underside of the lead lining can also lead to dampness and decay in roof timbers. Maintenance and repairs for valley gutters can be costly, making regular inspection and cleaning essential. Condition Rating NI. standard_paragraphs.label: Butterfly Roof Amend as appropriate
standard_paragraphs.text: Defective rainwater goods are a very common cause of dampness which can lead to deterioration in building fabric and the development of rot in timbers. Regular inspection and adequate maintenance are therefore essential if serious problems such as dry rot are to be avoided. As mentioned, it was not raining at the time of our inspection. We therefore cannot comment on the functionality of rainwater goods or surface water disposal. We are also unable to comment upon possible leakage. The gutters and downpipes should be observed during rain and any leaking joints resealed or replaced as necessary. The point of final discharge from the downpipes is unconfirmed, but is likely to discharge into the foul drainage system creating a “mixed” system which has existed for many years and is assumed not to contravene Local Authority requirements. As mentioned above, the roof is of butterfly construction. These roof structures utilise a horizontal valley gutter to direct rainwater runoff. The horizontal valley gutter feeds into a hopper head and a UPVC downpipe at the rear of the butterfly roof. The downpipe is fixed vertically to the external wall of the building, and where visible from the rear garden, the downpipe shoe appeared to discharge into the gutter serving the roof of the two-storey rear addition. The hopper head and downpipe at the rear of the building appear to be in good condition, with no significant defects observed. Condition Rating 1.

standard_paragraphs.label: Timber Ledger board deterioration
standard_paragraphs.text: There are timber beams at first-floor level on the front elevation, under the cladded wall, typically referred to as a ledger board or ribbon board. This horizontal timber component is fixed to the structural framing of the house and serves as support for the floor joists of the floor above. It also anchors the wall framing and provides stability to the structure. The ledger board plays a crucial role in connecting the floor system to the wall system and ensuring the overall integrity of the building. We noted signs of surface deterioration on the timber sections. This timber should be treated to resist moisture and pests. Condition Rating 2.

standard_paragraphs.text: There is no adequate provision for drainage in the external grounds. In heavy rain, this may cause water ponding, increasing the risk of penetrating dampness. A French drain should be installed to channel the water away to a suitable outlet. Previous recommendations for infilling with pea shingle have now been superseded, as it has been found that this finer material holds moisture. Condition Rating 3.

standard_paragraphs.label: French drain is required 1
standard_paragraphs.text: There is no adequate provision of drainage to external grounds and in heavy rain this may cause water ponding which increases the risk of penetrating dampness. A small trench should be dug around the external walls of the property. This need only be approximately 150 mm width from the wall and infilled with stones, ideally with a French Drain (perforated pipe) beneath this, channelling the water away to a suitable outlet. The previous recommendations for infilling with Pea Shingle have now been superseded as it has been found that this finer material in fact holds moisture. Condition Rating 2.

standard_paragraphs.label: History of underpinning
standard_paragraphs.text: There is a history of underpinning to the property. It should be noted that different lenders may have different policies and approaches towards properties with history of underpinning. For example, some high street lenders state that properties that have been subject to underpinning must have the residue of a 10 (some 20) year guarantee, evidence of full Building Regulations approval and be given a supportive valuation to be acceptable security to the Bank. Some state that in some cases it may be prudent only to accept underpinned terraced or semi-detached dwellings if the abutting ones have been similarly treated, or where it is proved that the proposed security is unaffected by a local or inherent individual problem. Also, some lenders do not accept properties which have been underpinned within the last 3 years. This is generally not welcomed by some lenders and therefore may affect the future saleability of the property. However, I did not note any visible signs of structural movement which indicates that any works have been functional so far. Your legal adviser should investigate and request the relevant documentation for the works that have been undertaken and ensure all remedial work is carried out under a long term and meaningful guarantee with a suitable insurance indemnity. It is imperative that the relevant documentation for this is requested to include Building Regulations approval.

Your solicitor should make further enquiries with the building management as to this matter. Whilst this is a worst-case scenario, these are the risks are something you should be aware of prior to purchase.

standard_paragraphs.label: On glazing
standard_paragraphs.text: There is a cat flap in the rear patio door. This appears unsightly, and you may wish to remove this. Removing a cat flap from patio door glazing without replacing the glazing is generally not possible. Cutting a hole in the glass for a cat flap compromises the structural integrity of the glass. Once a hole is made, the glass is permanently weakened, and removing the cat flap leaves an unrepairable hole. Cutting a hole for a cat flap can break the vacuum seal between the glass panes. This seal is critical for the insulation properties of the glazing, and once broken, it cannot be restored without replacing the glazing unit. Also, the resulting hole would be unsightly and could let in drafts, reducing the energy efficiency of the door. The most practical solution is to replace the entire glazing panel. This will restore the door to its original condition, maintaining its structural integrity, insulation properties, and aesthetic appearance. Condition

standard_paragraphs.label: Partly missing fascia board
standard_paragraphs.text: The fascia board at the rear is of UPVC construction. We are uncertain as to whether this is replacement unit, or capping over the original softwood. If softwood fascia is still in place, it could be subject to decay. The fascia board at the rear is incomplete and is not extending all across the rear gutter. This is a poor building practice and the work has been undertaken to a substandard quality. A section of the wall behind the gutter to the right is exposed. The fascia board should be extended however this work will require temporary removal of the hopper head and downpipe at the rear. Without an adequate fascia board, water from the gutter can seep behind the gutter and into the roof and walls of the house, causing water damage to the roofing structure, walls, and foundation. Also, Missing fascia boards can provide easy access points for pests and insects. In addition, missing fascia boards can compromise the structural integrity of the roof edge, leading to potential roof damage and instability of the gutter system. Water infiltration due to missing fascia boards can create moist conditions ideal for mold and mildew growth. Continuous exposure to water can lead to more frequent repairs and maintenance. Condition rating 2.
